Maleficent

muh-LEF-ih-sent -- from Latin male ('badly') + facere ('to do, make'). · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Maleficent is harmful or evil in intent or effect, especially in a menacing, almost magical way.

Local legend blamed the region's failed harvests on a maleficent spirit said to wander the orchard at night.

Worked Example

The old fairy tale describes a maleficent fairy who cursed the princess out of pure spite for not being invited to the celebration.

That kind of deliberately wicked, harm-intending force -- not just an accident, but genuine evil intent -- is exactly what maleficent describes.

How Maleficent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

harmful

harmful: causing damage or injury

sinister

sinister: suggesting evil intent in a way that feels menacing

Antonyms

benevolent

benevolent: kind and genuinely well-meaning

harmless

harmless: unable to cause any damage at all

How Strong Is It? — harmful → maleficent → sinister

harmful vs. maleficent

harmful vs. maleficent: Harmful is weaker than maleficent: loose nails in an old floor can cause harm by pure accident, while a maleficent act means damage done with genuine evil intent.

sinister vs. maleficent

sinister vs. maleficent: Sinister is graver than maleficent: a maleficent scheme sets out to do harm, but a sinister watcher by the playground radiates a deeper, more menacing kind of evil.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of maleficent.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — male-

Prefix — male-: badly, evil (Latin male)

Root — fic

Root — fic: to do, make (from Latin facere; the same root is spelled fac in malefactor)

Suffix — -ent

Suffix — -ent: adjective-forming, 'doing' (Latin -entem)

Put it together

Put it together: Male- ('badly, evil') + fic ('to do, make' — from Latin facere) + -ent (adjective-forming): someone maleficent is, quite literally, one who 'does badly,' or does evil on purpose.

Use the root in a new word: malefactor

Use the root in a new word: malefactor: The night watchman finally caught the malefactor who had been vandalizing the park benches.

Root Check

Word Choice

Maleficent is a strong, almost storybook word, usually reserved for a deliberately evil force, curse, or intention -- contrast it with the milder odious, taught later in this unit, which describes something that simply arouses hatred or disgust rather than active evil intent.
